clue.text: Look the worse for wear after a loud set-to

indicators.note: after places the opening phrase's word behind what follows it, so it is written second

blocks.note: taken as written
f is forte, the musical marking for loud
cloth that frays looks worn and tattered

explanation.surface: Someone looks battered after a noisy row.
explanation.walkthrough: The clue reads 'after' literally: the worn-looking word goes after the article and the loud sign.
explanation.definitionFit: An affray is a public fight or brawl, which is what a set-to is.

clue.text: Blood problem's on the rise, I imply in articles

indicators.note: in a down clue, rising means the letters are read upwards, so from the bottom
in places one piece inside the letters that surround it

blocks.note: A twice, the indefinite article, one at each end
to say 'I mean' is to imply something

explanation.surface: A patient hints that their blood complaint is getting worse.
explanation.definitionFit: Anaemia is a shortage of red blood cells or haemoglobin, a disorder of the blood.

clue.text: Note written by London college not reliable

blocks.note: fa is a note of the sol-fa scale
the London School of Economics

explanation.surface: A note from a London college turns out to be untrustworthy.
explanation.walkthrough: The LSE, the London School of Economics, is a well-known college of the University of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Something false cannot be trusted or depended upon, so it is unreliable.

clue.text: A new customer left out from the ark

indicators.note: when something is left out it is omitted, so this letter is dropped from the word

blocks.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
a client is a customer
L is the abbreviation for left

explanation.surface: A newcomer is missing from Noah's ark.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Out from the ark' looks like one phrase, but 'out' belongs to the wordplay and 'from the ark' is the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Something 'out of the ark' is jokingly old, as if dating from Noah's flood, i.e. very old.

clue.text: Speaker's last boring subject — "circle on sphere"

indicators.note: last asks for only the final letter of the word before it
something boring drills into another word, so it sits inside it

blocks.note: a topic is a subject under discussion
the final letter of speaker

explanation.surface: The last talker drones on about a dull subject, apparently circles on spheres.
explanation.definitionFit: The tropics of Cancer and Capricorn are lines of latitude, circles drawn on the globe.

clue.text: Perform liturgy going round church backwards

indicators.note: backwards tells you to read the abbreviation in the opposite direction
going round means one word wraps itself around another

blocks.note: a rite is a liturgical ceremony
CE is the Church of England

explanation.surface: A cleric performs the service while walking backwards around the church.
explanation.definitionFit: To recite is to deliver aloud from memory, a kind of performance.

clue.text: Number in charge not from South American university

indicators.note: in puts one thing inside another
in a down clue, reading from the south means starting at the bottom and going up

blocks.note: a charge is a price
N is the abbreviation for number
taken as written, then turned upwards

explanation.surface: Someone in charge of numbers is told they are not from a South American university.
explanation.walkthrough: 'South American' looks like one phrase; split it, as 'from South' is the turning signal and 'American university' the definition.
explanation.definitionFit: Princeton is an Ivy League university in New Jersey, USA.

clue.text: My uncle baselessly spread round a malicious lie

indicators.note: in a down clue the base is the bottom, so the last letter is dropped
spread out letters are scattered and rearranged
round means the rearranged letters go around the next piece

blocks.note: taken as written, then losing its final letter
taken as written

explanation.surface: My uncle spreads a malicious rumour without any grounds.
explanation.definitionFit: Calumny is a false and slanderous statement made to damage someone's reputation.

clue.text: Organising cull, academist slipped up

indicators.note: organising puts things into a new order, so the letters are rearranged

blocks.note: the letters of both words

explanation.surface: An academic got it wrong when organising a cull of animals.
explanation.definitionFit: To miscalculate is to make an error of judgement or arithmetic, to slip up.

clue.text: Stir trouble on 1st of January

indicators.note: the first of a word is its opening letter only

blocks.note: the opening letter of January
to ail is to trouble or afflict

explanation.surface: Stirring up trouble on New Year's Day.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Stir' is a verb in the surface but here it is slang for prison.
explanation.definitionFit: Stir is old slang for prison, a synonym of jail.

clue.text: Asian land invaded by unfriendly rodent

indicators.note: a land invaded by something has that thing inside its borders

blocks.note: China is a country in Asia
chill as an adjective means cold, unwelcoming

explanation.surface: An Asian country is overrun by a hostile rodent.
explanation.definitionFit: The chinchilla is a small South American rodent prized for its soft fur.

clue.text: Hobbled out of capital English bar

indicators.note: the capital is the head letter of a word, and out of means it is removed

blocks.note: to hobble is to limp
E is the abbreviation for English

explanation.surface: Someone limped out of the capital to an English pub.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Capital' suggests a city, but here it means the capital letter, the first one.
explanation.definitionFit: To bar something is to obstruct or block it, the verb sense matching impede.

clue.text: Place for dead feline and canine our mother buried, originally

indicators.note: originally points to the origin of each word, its first letter

blocks.note: a feline is a cat
the opening letters of these five words

explanation.surface: A family buries its dead cat and dog.
explanation.definitionFit: A catacomb is an underground cemetery, a place where the dead are laid.

clue.text: Bob possibly getting call after controversial musical

blocks.note: Hair, the 1960s rock musical, caused controversy with its nudity
to style is to call or name

explanation.surface: Bob gets a phone call after seeing a controversial show.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Bob' looks like a man's name, but it is the short haircut.
explanation.definitionFit: A bob is one example of a haircut, hence 'possibly' marking an example.

clue.text: Off-the-peg item eager assistant talked of?

indicators.note: something talked of is heard, so the sound counts and not the spelling

blocks.note: ready means willing, eager
a maid is a domestic assistant

explanation.surface: An eager shop assistant chatters about a ready-to-wear garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Off-the-peg clothes are mass-produced rather than tailored, i.e. bought ready to wear.

clue.text: Go off course, lacking right support

indicators.note: lacking means without, so that letter is taken away

blocks.note: to stray is to wander off the path
R is the abbreviation for right

explanation.surface: Something veers off course without proper support.
explanation.definitionFit: A stay is a prop or brace, such as a rope steadying a mast.

clue.text: Blow friends over

indicators.note: something turned over is flipped, so the letters run the other way

blocks.note: pals are friends

explanation.surface: A puff of air knocks some friends over.
explanation.definitionFit: A slap is a blow with the open hand.

clue.text: Portion proving adequate

blocks.note: first meaning: a helping of food
second meaning: answering a purpose, as in 'that will serve'

explanation.walkthrough: The surface reads as a meal being enough; the two halves are separate senses of one word.
explanation.definitionFit: A serving is a helping of food; serving also means doing duty or being suitable for a purpose.

clue.text: Genuine doctor in Utah etc

indicators.note: to doctor something is to tamper with it, so the letters are altered

blocks.note: all the letters of these three words

explanation.surface: A real physician practising in Utah and elsewhere.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Doctor' looks like a noun describing someone in Utah, but it is a verb telling you to rework the letters, 'in' included.
explanation.definitionFit: Authentic means real, not fake, the same as genuine.

clue.text: Practical husband and child

blocks.note: H is the abbreviation for husband
taken as written
a son is a child

explanation.surface: A sensible husband and his child.
explanation.definitionFit: A hands-on approach involves direct practical involvement rather than theory.

clue.text: I worried plenty, showing little skill

indicators.note: worried means harried and shaken about, so the letters are disturbed

blocks.note: the letters of I and plenty

explanation.surface: Someone frets a great deal, clumsily.
explanation.definitionFit: Doing something ineptly means doing it incompetently, with little skill.

clue.text: Takes in essential features of bridge

blocks.note: first meaning: deceives, fools
second meaning: in the card game bridge, the rounds of play won or lost

explanation.walkthrough: 'Bridge' suggests a structure, but it is the card game, where the play is counted in rounds of four cards.
explanation.definitionFit: To trick someone is to deceive them; in bridge, tricks are the rounds whose count decides the contract.

clue.text: Indistinct realm where OAPs hang out?

blocks.note: first meaning: an unclear situation not fitting a category
second meaning, whimsical: a zone for grey-haired people

explanation.walkthrough: OAP is British for old-age pensioner; the joke reads the idiom literally as a district for the grey-haired.
explanation.definitionFit: A grey area is an ill-defined situation; literally, pensioners with grey hair might gather there.

clue.text: Stolen with chips?

blocks.note: first meaning: British slang for pinched
second meaning: having small notches cut out of it

explanation.walkthrough: 'Chips' suggests food served with fish; here it means small nicks in a surface.
explanation.definitionFit: In British slang to nick is to steal; a nick is also a small cut or notch.

clue.text: Small part of poem accurately recalled

indicators.note: of here means taken out of, so the letters sit within the next words
recalled means called back, so the letters run backwards

blocks.note: the letters straddling the two words

explanation.surface: An actor remembers a short bit of verse word for word.
explanation.definitionFit: A cameo is a brief appearance by a well-known actor, a small part.

clue.text: More than one banker is in France, relaxing

indicators.note: relaxing loosens things up, so the letters fall into a new order

blocks.note: every letter of the three words

explanation.surface: A banker is on holiday in France.
explanation.definitionFit: Financiers are people who deal in large-scale finance, such as bankers, plural to match.

clue.text: Mounties regularly struck dumb

indicators.note: regularly means at even intervals, taking every other letter

blocks.note: the first, third, fifth and seventh letters

explanation.surface: The Canadian police are often left speechless.
explanation.walkthrough: Mounties are the Royal Canadian Mounted Police.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone mute is silent, as if struck dumb and unable to speak.

clue.text: Obsequious Greek making few demands

blocks.note: GR is the abbreviation for Greek
something easy makes few demands

explanation.surface: A fawning Greek who is undemanding.
explanation.definitionFit: Greasy can mean ingratiating or unctuous, like an oily flatterer.

clue.text: Pretentious name adopted by puppet

indicators.note: something adopted is taken in, so it goes inside

blocks.note: Sooty is a yellow bear glove puppet from British children's television
N is the abbreviation for name

explanation.surface: A puppet takes on a grand-sounding name.
explanation.walkthrough: Sooty is a famous British glove puppet bear.
explanation.definitionFit: Snooty means snobbish and condescending, behaving with pretension.
